record-contents.title: CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events

ocsf_activity.format: One of a small closed set of captions; the id is the same fact as a number.

Unknown.meaning: activity_id 0: not mapped to one of the named activities.

Create.meaning: activity_id 1: the API call pertains to a create activity.

Read.meaning: activity_id 2: the API call pertains to a read activity.

Update.meaning: activity_id 3: the API call pertains to an update activity.

Delete.meaning: activity_id 4: the API call pertains to a delete activity.

Other.meaning: activity_id 99: an activity not covered by Create/Read/Update/Delete.

ocsf_category.format: One fixed caption for this sourcetype.

Application Activity.meaning: category_uid 6: application and API-level activity, as opposed to network or findings categories.

ocsf_class.format: One fixed caption for this sourcetype.

API Activity.meaning: class_uid 6003: general CRUD API activity, OCSF's example being AWS CloudTrail.

ocsf_type.format: Derived: type_uid = class_uid*100 + activity_id (600300-600304, 600399); type_name is class_name and activity_name joined by a colon.

ocsf_severity.format: One fixed word, case-sensitive; the id is the same fact as a number.

Low.meaning: severity_id 2: the user decides if action is needed.

Medium.meaning: Severity_id 3 in the OCSF scale: a response is expected, though nothing urgent.
Medium.quote: severity_id 3: action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

Critical.meaning: OCSF severity_id 5, one tier under the top: needs an immediate look, and the blast radius reaches wide.

Fatal.meaning: OCSF severity_id 6, the scale's very top: whatever broke, the window for a fix already closed.

ocsf_status.format: The caption of an unobserved status_id: Success, Failure or Other/Unknown. status_id itself is not in this sourcetype's observed field list; only the status caption is.

event_time.format: time is epoch seconds; time_dt is the same instant as an ISO 8601 datetime string.

actor_user_type.format: One of a closed AWS-defined set; not itself repeated on the OCSF User object page as an enum (User.type is a free string there), but its literal values are CloudTrail's own userIdentity.type set.

Root.meaning: The request was made with the AWS account's own (root) credentials.

IAMUser.meaning: The caller authenticated as a named IAM user, not an assumed role or a service.
IAMUser.quote: The request was made with the credentials of an IAM user.

AssumedRole.meaning: The request used temporary credentials obtained by assuming an IAM role via STS AssumeRole.

Role.meaning: The request used a persistent IAM role identity; the role itself is the session issuer.

FederatedUser.meaning: The request used temporary credentials from STS GetFederationToken.

AWSAccount.meaning: A different AWS account, not this one, is the identity that assumed into a role here.

AWSService.meaning: An AWS service itself, not a human or a role, is the identity behind this call.

IdentityCenterUser.meaning: A person signed in through IAM Identity Center is behind this call, not a raw IAM credential.

Unknown.meaning: CloudTrail could not determine the identity type.

session_uid.format: uid is an opaque session id; uid_alt is the session's ARN form for an assumed role.

examples.note: uid_alt, from the OCSF Session object's own example.

observable_type.format: One of a closed set of 31 literals; abbreviated here to the ones plausible for CloudTrail-sourced API Activity events (full table at the cite URL). Left out: 23 of 31 OCSF type_id literals (MAC Address, Email Address, URL String, File Name, Hash, Process Name, Port, Subnet, Command Line, Country, Process ID, HTTP User-Agent, CWE/CVE object uids, Email, URL, File, Process, Geo Location, Container, Registry Key/Value, Fingerprint, Unknown) documented at the cite URL but not plausible on a CloudTrail-shaped event.

IP Address.meaning: type_id 2: an IPv4 or IPv6 address.

Resource UID.meaning: type_id 10: a resource unique identifier, for example an S3 bucket name or EC2 instance id.

User Credential ID.meaning: type_id 19: a credential's unique id, for example an AWS access key id.

Endpoint.meaning: type_id 20: a physical or virtual device on the network.

User.meaning: type_id 21: characteristics of a user or security principal.

Other.meaning: type_id 99: not mapped to a named type.

unmapped_management_event.quote: identifies whether the event is a management event

true.meaning: Marks an API call, such as DescribeTrails, that reads state and changes nothing.
true.quote: The operation is read-only, for example DescribeTrails.

false.meaning: The operation writes, for example DeleteTrail.

unmapped_session_cred_console.format: true or false; CloudTrail omits the field entirely unless the value is true.
unmapped_session_cred_console.quote: shows whether or not an event originated from an AWS Management Console session

unmapped_session_issuer_type.format: One of a closed set, narrower than the top-level userIdentity.type set (no AssumedRole, FederatedUser or IdentityCenterUser: the issuer is always the credential's origin).

Root.meaning: The session's credentials trace back to the AWS account's own (root) credentials.

IAMUser.meaning: The session's credentials trace back to an IAM user.

Role.meaning: The session's credentials trace back to assuming an IAM role.

unmapped_addl_amz_id2.format: An opaque S3 trace id string.
